explanation: Perform the first k steps of a uniform shuffle without constructing all n entries. A dictionary records only virtual positions changed by swaps, giving distinct uniformly selected values.
timeComplexity: O(k) expected dictionary time. Each of k iterations performs a constant number of expected-time hash operations; at most O(k) map entries are introduced.
spaceComplexity: O(k), including the returned subset. At most a constant number of virtual-map entries are added per selection, plus k output entries.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: The map implements the first k swaps of a virtual Fisher–Yates shuffle: unmapped positions still contain their own indices. Each step chooses uniformly from the unselected suffix and moves its chosen value into the result. The ordered sample is uniform; each unordered k-element subset has exactly k! orders, so all subsets have equal probability.
walkthrough: For n=5 and k=2, one possible run chooses virtual position 3, then position 4. It returns [3,4], recording the displaced virtual values only where necessary. Every two-element subset of {0,1,2,3,4} has probability 1/10, regardless of returned order. JSON arguments are [n,k]. Observed true is the property/distribution check, not the callable return.
edgeCases: k=n returns every value in some order.
No selected value can appear twice.
